newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti suit against ex-manager adjourned.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti suit against ex-manager adjourned.

text.p: A civil suit for damages brought by Italian information and technology group Olivetti against an ex-manager formally opened on Wednesday but was adjourned until May.
Olivetti is suing its former director-general in charge of finance and auditing Renzo Francesconi for 100 billion lire damages after he cast doubts on the group's accounts.
Only the lawyers for both sides were present for the start of the hearing.

Francesconi resigned in early September after only two months at Olivetti after he questioned the accuracy of first half 1996 accounts just one day after the results were made public. Olivetti announced a six-month pre-tax loss of 440.2 billion lire.
Olivetti said it was seeking damages after Francesconi's comments which led to the suspension of Olivetti stock trading after excessive share price falls.

His comments "provoked serious upsets on the financial market, causing very heavy damage to the company and leading to the intervention of the stock exchange regulator Consob," Olivetti said in its suit.
